_comment: Customs codes used to measure EU-bound trade in CBAM goods. Feeds eu_export_share. Read at runtime; never hardcode (KARBON_ATLASI.md section 7).

meta.authoritative_source: Regulation (EU) 2023/956, ANNEX I — List of goods and greenhouse gases, Official Journal L 130, 16.5.2023, pages 90-93
meta.scope_note: Transcribed 2026-09-06 from the Official Journal PDF itself, pages L 130/90 to L 130/93 — not from a summary or a consultancy list. The earlier HS2/HS4 aggregates have been replaced. Three real differences were found against them: cement was missing 2507 00 80 entirely; iron and steel was missing 2601 12 00 and carried chapter 72 without Annex I's ferro-alloy and scrap carve-outs; aluminium carried the whole of chapter 76, which Annex I does not — it excludes 7602 (waste and scrap) and 7615 (table, kitchen and household articles).
meta.query_note: THE LIST IS VERIFIED; THE QUERY DOES NOT YET APPLY IT. 01b_fetch_eu_trade.R still asks Comext for the broad headings and cannot subtract the `exclusions` arrays below, so any eu_export_share derived from it remains an UPPER BOUND for iron and steel and for aluminium. Cement is unaffected: Annex I lists all five 2523 subheadings, so the HS4 aggregate and the CN8 list coincide there, and only 2507 00 80 had to be added. Applying the exclusions means querying at CN8 and summing the included codes, which is a change to 01b, not to this file.

trade_source.dataset: DS-045409 — EU trade since 1988 by HS2-4-6 and CN8

dimension_codes.flow: 1 (IMPORT — i.e. EU imports FROM Türkiye, which is Türkiye's export TO the EU)

trade_source.unit_note: QUANTITY_IN_100KG is in hundreds of kilograms. Divide by 10 to obtain tonnes.

cement.description: Other kaolinic clays; cement clinkers; white Portland cement; other Portland cement; aluminous cement; other hydraulic cements.
cement.annex_i_note: Complete and exact. Annex I lists all five 2523 subheadings, so the previous HS4 aggregate `2523` was not an overstatement — it was simply missing 2507 00 80, which is a clay rather than a cement and is easy to overlook.

iron-and-steel.code_level: chapter 72 with carve-outs, plus CN8 and HS4 headings
iron-and-steel.description: Chapter 72 in full except the listed ferro-alloys and ferrous scrap, plus agglomerated iron ores (2601 12 00) and the chapter 73 headings Annex I brings into scope.
iron-and-steel.annex_i_note: `72022` is Annex I's own '7202 2 — Ferro-silicon', a five-digit subheading group rather than a CN8 code; it is stored as written. 7204 is ferrous waste and scrap. Until 01b subtracts these, the steel figure is an upper bound.

aluminum.description: Unwrought aluminium, powders, bars, wire, plates, foil, tubes, fittings, structures, reservoirs, casks, containers, stranded wire and other articles.
aluminum.annex_i_note: Chapter 76 as a whole was an overstatement: Annex I omits 7602 (waste and scrap) and 7615 (table, kitchen and household articles). Note the gases — aluminium is the ONLY sector here carrying perfluorocarbons, and Climate TRACE publishes no PFC country package, so aluminium exposure computed by this project is an underestimate by an unknown margin.

out_of_scope.fertilisers: Covered by CBAM (Annex I) but excluded from this project: no open source publishes Turkish fertiliser-production facilities. See ROADMAP.md.
out_of_scope.electricity: Covered by CBAM. Excluded by choice: Turkish electricity exports to the EU are marginal.
out_of_scope.hydrogen: Covered by CBAM. Excluded by choice: negligible volume.
